lifecycle.pivot_impact_2026_08_16: PIVOT IMPACT 2026-08-16: this microtask was written against PostgreSQL. Its premise - isolated PER-TEST POSTGRESQL SCHEMA teardown and a 1009-schema backlog to reclaim - no longer exists. PostgreSQL has been physically deleted from the product (storage/postgres.rs, managed_postgres.rs, the .sqlx cache and the sqlx dependency are gone) and Handshake now uses an EMBEDDED SurrealDB store whose test isolation is a per-run HANDSHAKE_DATA_DIR directory, not a schema name. There are no schemas to leak and no pg_class rows to count, so proof targets PT-123-1 (schema count, pg_class relation count, cluster directory size) and PT-123-3 (parallel-run schema reclamation) are VOID as written. The underlying risk is REAL and CARRIED FORWARD: an aborted test process can still leave an embedded store directory behind, and crash-safe teardown plus reclamation of orphaned stores is still required. The 2026-08-13 session already began this work - tests/surreal_test_store_crash_safety_tests.rs and tests/surreal_test_store_support/ exist and are committed. This contract must be re-scoped to the embedded store before implementation resumes: restate the acceptance criteria and proof targets in terms of store DIRECTORIES, and note that the six acceptance_criteria entries below are empty in the source contract and must be authored.

scope.summary: RESCOPED 2026-08-16 from PostgreSQL to the embedded SurrealDB store. The original microtask targeted isolated per-test POSTGRESQL SCHEMA teardown and a 1009-schema backlog; PostgreSQL has been physically deleted, so there are no schemas to leak and no pg_class rows to count. THE UNDERLYING RISK IS UNCHANGED AND STILL REAL, which is why this is rescoped rather than closed: test isolation now comes from a per-run HANDSHAKE_DATA_DIR directory containing a handshake-surreal RocksDB store, and a test process that is killed or panics mid-run strands that directory on disk. Each store is measured in hundreds of megabytes to gigabytes, so a stranded-store backlog degrades proof runs and consumes the artifacts volume exactly the way the schema backlog did. Prior work exists and must be built on, not duplicated: tests/surreal_test_store_crash_safety_tests.rs and tests/surreal_test_store_support/ were created by the 2026-08-13 session and are committed. RocksDB holds an exclusive LOCK file while a store is open, and SurrealStorage::shutdown on Windows already waits until that LOCK is re-acquirable, so LOCK acquirability is the available liveness signal for deciding whether a store directory is genuinely orphaned or still owned by a live run.

Each isolated schema materializes the full migration set, so one leaked schema costs ~1793 relations.
defect_detail.teardown_exists_but_is_not_crash_safe: knowledge_pg_support.rs DOES implement teardown - drop_schema_sql (:41), drop_and_verify_schema (:48) which verifies the schema is really gone (:90), and teardown_inner (:170) with an explicit note that an outstanding PoolConnection must not make teardown wait forever. So this is NOT missing cleanup. The failure mode is that teardown only runs when the test process survives to run it. This work packet has a documented history of test processes being killed mid-run (MT-119 implementation_result records a platform session limit killing all three launched agents within minutes, the sixth such outage that session). Every killed run leaves a full ~1793-relation schema behind permanently.
defect_detail.verification_still_required: Confirm whether any live process currently owns a knowledge_test_ schema before reclaiming, and whether other databases in this 27-database cluster carry the same backlog. The counts above are for database handshake only.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test store directory is reclaimable after the owning process dies without running any teardown code. Reclamation must not depend on a graceful shutdown path, because the whole failure mode is that the process never reached one.

Reclamation NEVER removes a store belonging to a live run. Ownership is decided from an observable liveness signal - the RocksDB LOCK file is exclusively held while a store is open - and not from age heuristics or a naming convention alone. A concurrent proof run must survive a reclamation pass untouched.

Reclamation is safe under concurrency: two reclamation passes running at once, or a reclamation racing a starting run, must not delete a store that the starting run is about to open, and must not double-delete.

Reclamation is bounded and reports what it did: how many store directories were examined, how many were reclaimed, how many were skipped as live, and how much space was freed. A silent pass is not acceptable, because a reclaimer that quietly does nothing is indistinguishable from one that works.

Reclamation stays inside the artifacts root and refuses any path outside it, so a misconfigured HANDSHAKE_DATA_DIR can never point the reclaimer at the repository, the governance runtime root, or an operator directory.
The existing surreal_test_store_support harness gains the teardown path so ordinary tests inherit it, rather than each test having to remember to clean up. Existing tests keep passing unchanged.

proof_targets: PT-123-1: a killed-process proof - spawn a child that opens a store and kill it without teardown, then show the directory stranded and subsequently reclaimed, with before/after directory listings and byte counts captured verbatim.

PT-123-2: a live-run safety proof - run reclamation while a store is open and show that store survives, then show it becomes reclaimable after its owner exits. This is the counterfactual that proves AC-123-2 is not vacuous.
PT-123-3: a containment proof - point the reclaimer at a path outside the artifacts root and show it refuses rather than deleting.
PT-123-4: the reclamation report showing examined / reclaimed / skipped-live counts and bytes freed, from a real run.
scope.risk_if_missed: Every PostgreSQL-backed proof in this and future work packets pays a growing startup tax, and an unclean shutdown can cost 15+ minutes before any work can start. It also inflates the artifact footprint the Operator asked to keep optimal.

hbr_obligations.SWARM: Reclamation runs against a cluster shared by parallel work packets. The ownership predicate is the safety-critical part of this MT.

risks: A reclaimer that deletes by age or filename pattern will eventually delete a live run store during a slow proof and produce a failure that looks like a product defect.
A reclaimer walking outside the artifacts root could delete repository or governance state; this is the highest-severity failure in this microtask and is why AC-123-5 exists.
A reclaimer that reports nothing cannot be distinguished from one that silently does nothing, so the backlog would grow again unnoticed.
Reclamation racing a starting run could delete a directory between creation and open.
minimum_controls: AC-123-2 plus PT-123-2 require a live-store counterfactual, not just a happy-path deletion.
AC-123-5 plus PT-123-3 require a refusal proof for paths outside the artifacts root.
AC-123-4 plus PT-123-4 require a report with real counts.

findings.failure_scenario: A misconfigured or hostile HANDSHAKE_TEST_STORE_ROOT, or any direct sweep_stale_orphans caller, can designate an arbitrary real directory as the trusted root. prepare_root creates/canonicalizes that directory and the reclaimer then treats matching store-* children as eligible; the contracted outer containment boundary is therefore absent even though nested reparse containment is implemented.
remediation: Resolve one canonical artifacts root through the existing Handshake artifact-root configuration and make the default test-store root a descendant of that root; remove the std::env::temp_dir fallback.

Change sweep_stale_orphans/prepare_root so the canonical artifacts root is an independent authority input, not the same caller-controlled path being validated. Canonicalize the authority root first and reject an empty, missing, non-directory, reparse, non-canonical, or outside candidate root before creating, enumerating, renaming, or deleting anything.

Require the canonical candidate root to be equal to or a strict descendant of the canonical artifacts root using path-component-aware comparison; preserve the existing immediate-child, identity, ownership-marker, quarantine, and nested reparse checks beneath that accepted boundary.

Add PT-123-3 as a direct negative test: create a sentinel directory outside the canonical artifacts root containing a matching store-* candidate, call the public reclaimer with that directory, require InvalidInput/typed refusal, and prove the sentinel tree and metadata remain unchanged. Also prove a nonexistent outside path is not created.
Add a configuration test proving configured_test_store_root() resolves under the canonical artifacts root both with normal configuration and with a rejected outside override.

Rerun the killed-owner reclamation, live-owner survival, dual-sweeper/startup race, bounded-report/bytes-freed, ordinary harness teardown, and new outside-root refusal proofs against isolated managed SurrealDB stores.
findings.pass_conditions: The public reclaimer cannot create, enumerate, quarantine, or delete outside the independently resolved canonical Handshake artifacts root; PT-123-3 produces a typed refusal with an untouched external sentinel; the default and configured store roots are artifact-contained; and all existing crash, liveness, concurrency, accounting, and inherited teardown proofs remain green.
